title: Buy a home gym, escape the Gestapo
summary: NH argues the main reason to build a home gym is escaping people: chatty gym-goers, equipment sharers and especially gym staff who policed his deadlifts, threatened bans and called the police. A gym should be loud and focused; at some point an elite physique needs its own gym, and needing others to train shows a lack of discipline.
claims: With home gyms normalized, competition has cut prices, so it is now a good time to build one
Other gym-goers are the biggest thing slowing your progress in a commercial gym
To build an elite physique you eventually need your own personal gym; sharing does not work long term
Chatty members kill your flow and focus, especially between heavy deadlift reps
Sharing a squat rack with a much shorter lifter forces you to wreck your setup every set
He nearly got banned for deadlifting: staff claimed he damaged the floor, scared people, and called the police on him several times
If a gym posts 'no grunting, no dropping weights', leave; it is a library pretending to be a gym
Staff who do not lift tell members to lower deadlifts slowly; a staff member targeting him forced him to learn her schedule to deadlift
At home you can slam weights, grunt, blast music and train shirtless; a gym is not supposed to be quiet
Socializing in the gym means you are not training; a partner should only spot, help move weight and change plates
Pooling money with friends to build a shared neighborhood gym is a good solution if you need company
If you need other people to progress, you lack discipline
Looking at women in yoga pants is not a testosterone boost; it shifts your focus off the weights
A good home gym can be built with modest funds and less space than you think
